# Plan: SPE round r01, triage agent

This is round r01. No `spe/` folder exists and no triage agent exists yet. The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." The spec leaves a lot open, so I picked defaults. I log each default in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` so you can overrule any of them. Main defaults: the agent is a Python script that calls the Anthropic Messages API, it reads one support ticket and returns a category and a priority as JSON, and the test set is synthetic because I have no real tickets.

## 0. Before any writes

1. I confirm that pwd, the git remote, and `git status` match this repository. I also check that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. I check that it exists and never print its value.
2. I check the current Anthropic docs for the Sonnet and Opus model IDs and their prices. I write them to `spe/evals/harness/prices.yaml`. If a price differs from my assumption in section 2, I recompute that cost band before the predictions are saved and note the change in the yaml.

## 1. Specify

**Transcript.** `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` holds your prompt and your planning answers verbatim. I never edit it.

**Requirements.** I write this table to `spe/spec/spec.md` under "Round r01".

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns one category from: bug, feature_request, billing, account_access, how_to. | "triage tickets" + default D1 | `check_category` |
| R2 | The agent assigns one priority from P1 to P4. | "triage tickets" + default D2 | `check_priority` |
| R3 | Category accuracy is at least 0.85 on the scored set. | "correctly" + default D3 | `check_category` |
| R4 | P1 recall is at least 0.95. Missing an urgent ticket is the worst error. | "correctly" + default D4 | `check_p1_recall` |
| R5 | Mean cost per ticket is at most $0.005. | "cheaply" + default D5 | `check_cost` |
| R6 | Every output is valid JSON that matches the schema. | Decision: downstream systems need parseable output | `check_schema` |
| R7 | The agent sees only the ticket text. It never sees labels, graders, or predictions. | Decision: eval hygiene | transcript peek scan |

No earlier round exists, so there are no proposals to adopt or reject.

**Open decisions and defaults.** I write these to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.

| ID | Decision | Default used in r01 | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Category set | The 5 categories in R1 | You. Logged default. |
| D2 | Priority scale | P1 to P4. P1 means outage, data loss, security, or a blocked paying customer. | You. Logged default. |
| D3 | Category accuracy bar | 0.85 | You. Logged default. |
| D4 | P1 recall bar | 0.95 | You. Logged default. |
| D5 | Cost bar | $0.005 per ticket | You. Logged default. |
| D6 | Real tickets versus synthetic tickets | Synthetic set of 60 scored tickets | You. Open. Real tickets would change every number. |
| D7 | Add a Haiku configuration | Not included. I do not pick Haiku on my own. | You. Open. It is the obvious cheap arm for r02. |
| D8 | Paid API budget for the run | $10 cap | You. Logged default. |

## 2. Predict

**Configurations.** Each configuration changes one thing from A.

| Config | Model | Prompt | What changed from A |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sonnet | Zero-shot system prompt with category and priority definitions | Baseline |
| B | Sonnet | A's prompt plus 8 worked examples | Few-shot examples |
| C | Opus | A's prompt | Model |

Every configuration uses forced tool use for the JSON output, the SDK default temperature, and no prompt caching.

**Predictions.** A hit means the measured mean falls inside the band.

| Metric | A | B | C | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.86 ± 0.05 | 0.90 ± 0.04 | 0.89 ± 0.04 | `check_category` | The 5 categories are distinct. Most errors will be on how_to versus bug. Examples resolve that boundary better than a bigger model. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.70 ± 0.08 | 0.76 ± 0.07 | 0.74 ± 0.07 | `check_priority` | Priority is more subjective than category. P2 versus P3 will cause most misses. |
| P1 recall | 0.90 ± 0.07 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | `check_p1_recall` | Models tend to under-call urgency when the ticket tone is calm. Only 12 P1 tickets exist, so the bands are wide. |
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 1.00 ± 0.01 | `check_schema` | Forced tool use constrains the output shape. |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD) | 0.0040 ± 0.0015 | 0.0070 ± 0.0020 | 0.0065 ± 0.0020 | `check_cost` | Assumes about 900 input and 80 output tokens for A. B adds about 1,500 input tokens of examples. Prices assumed are $3/$15 per million tokens for Sonnet and $5/$25 for Opus, checked in step 0.2. |
| Requirements passed (of R3 to R6) | 3 ± 1 | 3 ± 1 | 3 ± 1 | all checks above | A should fail P1 recall. B and C should fail cost. |

I predict that no configuration passes every requirement in r01. The tension is between accuracy and cost. The naive guess is that B and C score the same as A on every metric. The close-out compares that naive guess with my predictions.

## 3. After approval, before anything else

1. I copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
2. I write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds round r01, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the 3 configurations, every number with its band and its Why, and `same_as_last_round: null` because no earlier round exists.
3. I commit locally: `SPE r01 specify` (transcript, spec.md, disagreements.md), then `SPE r01 predict: 3 configs, no config predicted to pass all requirements` (plan copy, predictions yaml, prices.yaml).

I never edit `r01.yaml` after a trial runs.

## 4. Build the agent and the harness

All of this work happens after the predict commit.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `triage/triage.py` | Reads one ticket from stdin. Calls the API with the config's model and prompt. Prints JSON with category, priority, input_tokens, and output_tokens. |
| `triage/configs/{A,B,C}.yaml` | Model ID and prompt file for each configuration |
| `triage/run_batch.py` | Runs one configuration over the ticket file. Writes one JSONL line per ticket. Stops when the budget file says the cap would be crossed. |
| `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` | Ticket ID and text only |
| `spe/evals/answers/gold.jsonl` | Gold labels. The triage agent and trial agents never read this file. |
| `spe/evals/graders/grade.py` | Code checks: `check_schema`, `check_category`, `check_priority`, `check_p1_recall`, `check_cost` |
| `spe/evals/graders/selftest.py` | Grader selftest |
| `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` | The round's Workflow script with `const ROUND = "r01"` |

**Dataset.** One subagent writes 72 tickets with labels. A second subagent labels the same tickets blind. I drop every ticket where the two labelers disagree and log it. I keep 60 scored tickets with 12 per category. The priority mix is 12 P1, 16 P2, 22 P3, and 10 P4. I do not write the gold labels myself, and I do not write the few-shot examples from the scored set.

**Judges.** r01 has no LLM judge. Code checks cover every metric.

Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.

## 5. Evaluate: the Workflow run

**Gates before launch.** The run halts if any gate fails.

1. Grader selftest. Gold labels as output score 1.00 on every check. Empty output fails every check. Shifted labels fail `check_category` and `check_priority`.
2. Regrade of last round as a control. No earlier round exists, so I log this gate as "N/A in r01". Round r02 regrades r01.
3. Dry run on 2 cells: config A and config C on 5 tickets each. I confirm that outputs parse, cost is recorded, and the peek scan runs.

**Workflow arguments.**

```json
{
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C"],
  "trials_per_cell": 3,
  "extra_trials_cap": 2,
  "split_threshold": 0.10,
  "api_budget_usd": 10,
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl",
  "dry_run_cells": ["A", "C"]
}
```

The round lives only in `ROUND` inside the script. Prompt text reads the round from that constant.

**Trial rules.**

- A trial is one full pass of one configuration over the 60 tickets. Each trial agent runs `triage/run_batch.py` and returns a fixed schema: config, trial number, output file path, ticket count, total tokens, and errors.
- Code grades every trial after it finishes. The trial agent does not grade.
- I scan every trial transcript for `spe/evals/answers`, `spe/evals/graders`, `spe/predictions`, and `gold`. I void any trial that touched them and log the void.
- Before each API call, `run_batch.py` checks spend against the $10 cap. It skips calls that would cross the cap and logs each skip.
- A cell is split when its trials differ by more than 0.10 on category accuracy or P1 recall. A split cell gets up to 2 extra trials.
- After grading, a failure-analysis agent reads every wrong label and groups the errors into F-numbered failure types. A completeness critic then checks that every prediction cell has a measured number and that every skip and void is logged.

**Cost estimate (not measured).** The run makes 9 trials of 60 calls, which is 540 API calls. That is about $1.75 at the predicted per-ticket costs. The maximum with all extra trials is 15 trials and about $2.90. The Workflow's own agent tokens for dataset building, trials, analysis, and the critic should be about 1.5 to 3 million tokens. That figure is a guess.

Commit when the run finishes: `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

## 6. Close-out

The Workflow returns at launch. I close out when its completion notice arrives.

- `spe/prediction-log.md` gets the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I say plainly if the naive guess beat my predictions.
- `spe/failures.md` gets an entry for each new failure type: name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. Original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md` gets a "Proposed for round r02" table. Likely candidates are prompt caching for B, a Haiku arm if you approve D7, and a P1 escalation rule.
- `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` is marked `status: draft`.
- `spe/README.md` gets updated.
- Commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and add the local tag `spe-r01`.

## 7. Commits, stops, and halts

- All commits are local. I do not push, deploy, or send anything.
- The commit order is `SPE r01 specify`, `SPE r01 predict`, `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`, `SPE r01 evaluate (results)`, `SPE r01 learn`, then the tag `spe-r01`.
- I halt and report if the budget cap is hit, an answer key leaks, the grader selftest fails, or a decision only you can make comes up (D6 or D7).
- The loop stops when predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row. If every configuration passes everything, round r02 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
critiques: Section 1 quotes the prompt "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" as the spec. It splits the prompt into requirements R1 to R7, and each row has a Test column such as `check_category`, `check_p1_recall`, `check_cost`, and the transcript peek scan.
The Predictions table gives number bands for configs A, B, and C on every metric. Examples are category accuracy 0.86 ± 0.05 for A and mean cost 0.0070 ± 0.0020 for B. No row uses adjectives.
Every metric row has a Why column. The cost Why states the token and price assumptions. The P1 recall Why says calm-toned tickets get under-called and that there are only 12 P1 tickets.
